It has a life of its own, in scrapbooks, on walls, in cardboard boxes, as long as the paper exists. Barthes likes the fact that what he sees has existed in front of the lens. The past is as certain as the present. He can assure himself of his mother and know that his experience with her was real. The Winter Garden image becomes a magic relic, as though it is part of his mother. It is interesting that Barthes settled on the Winter Garden Photograph as the Total Portrait. texts.full_text: MHz of Helix aspersa neurons causes a decrease of membrane resconductance. However, when the cells are exposed to microwave radiation at room temperate (20°C), an enhancement is observed in their input conductances for about two minutes after switching off microwaves. This study investigates whether this phenomenon can be explained by temperature effects and also examines how long these enhancements persist under various conditions of membrane potential. The results show that the magnitude as well as duration, up to 20 min., at which microwave-induced enhancement persists is influenced not only on cell position within irradiated field but more significantly affected through variations in initial temperatures. This indicates a significant role for temperature changes due microwaves exposure during experimental conditions or natural environments. Thus this phenomenon might be explained by local heat production and the resultant thermal gradients, leading to an increase of membrane conductance following microwave radiation at 2450 MHz which is associated with non-thermal effects in Helix aspersa neurons. Please note that further research needs conducted for understanding these findings fully; including more specific experimental design aimed exclusively on temperature-induced changes without exposure microwaves. This will help elucidate whether the observed enhancement of membrane conductance after microwave irradiation is primarily due to thermal or non-thermal effects, providing a clearer insight into how and why such phenomena occur in biological systems exposed at these frequencies.
